title: Aristotle's Three Appeals: Ethos, Pathos, Logos
explainer: In the Rhetoric, Aristotle analyzed persuasive speech as resting on three distinct appeals: the speaker's credibility (ethos), the audience's emotion (pathos), and the logical argument itself (logos). A technical talk or write-up that presents only facts and results is using just one of the three levers Aristotle identified over two thousand years ago — a useful check when preparing to present work to an audience that needs to be convinced, not just informed.
